Absolutely delusional. Anyone who has played that era of consoles knows, without question, the PS2 is vastly underpowered compared to the Xbox and the GameCube.

GTA 3 ran at 640x448i (PS2 resolutions ranged around 640x224 or 512x222 on most titles outside the few that had progressive 640x480) on PS2 with severe framerate drops to single digits. It could run 640x480 native or even 1280x720 at a locked 30FPS on Xbox with better graphical effects than PC's (Which was even a problem for high powered PC's though it wasn't the most well optimized game as the Xbox version used a lot of Nvidia specific tricks). Or if you go to GC, it ran almost every game at 640x480 locked. The difference between Need For Speed Underground on PS2 and GC is night and day. GC runs it unlocked 30FPS and at 640x480. PS2 below 30FPS at 512x444i.

There was a 50% gap between PS2 and GC and GC wiped the floor with it on anything outside heavy physics work (The only advantage PS2 had and the reason there was no GC version of Burnout 3). The gap is far bigger than 80%. The Xbox can often double PS2 framerates at 480p. And those tend to be the quick and dirty ports. When taken advantage of, the Xbox ran games that were impossible on PS2 -- basically what could be termed a generational gap.

GameCube was strong kit with a few downsides, at least relative to Xbox. The Flipper was a fixed-function GPU -- basically DX7 class -- it had split ram, and the Gekko wasn't SIMD. The latter may be the biggest flaw. Both PS2 and Xbox have SIMD CPUs; when people say the PowerPC in Gekko is superior to the P3 coppermine in Xbox, they have no idea what they are talking about. The P3 in Xbox wipes the floor with both PS2 and GameCube.

While Doom 3 was only possible on Xbox because of full, fat normal mapping, Half-Life 2 was dependent on the SSE CPU. The Xbox was the only console capable of the heavy physics load at that time.

Both the PS2 ane GC would choke on Halo: CE, let alone Half-Life 2.

Anything done on the PS4 today can be done on the XB1 by dropping the resolution some. This is the reality of both systems being cheap PCs internally.
